chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies leaving behind his maternal uncle, maternal aunt, paternal uncle, paternal aunt, daughter, and sister. He said: 'All of these inherit and take possession. When the paternal aunt and maternal aunt are together, the paternal aunt gets two-thirds and the maternal aunt gets one-third.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a paternal aunt versus a maternal aunt in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the concurrent inheritance rights of paternal and maternal aunts alongside other heirs, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence regarding the *Asabah* and *Dhawi al-Furud*. It specifically establishes the principle of *tarjih* (preference), where the paternal aunt (*ammah*) receives double the share of the maternal aunt (*khalah*) when both are present, reflecting the stronger paternal lineage in inheritance distribution. This ruling is derived from the general Quranic framework but specifies the proportional division not explicitly detailed in the primary verses.
